title: Steady one-dimensional conduction through a plane wall
decision_or_claim: Derive wall temperature and heat flux from prescribed face temperatures without calibration.
event_definition: A steady solution satisfies the energy equation and both face temperatures with zero volumetric generation.
system_boundary: Homogeneous solid slab from x=0 to x=L; the two faces are external boundaries and lateral faces are adiabatic by symmetry/large-aspect-ratio assumption.

regime.description: Continuum, stationary solid, steady one-dimensional conduction with constant isotropic conductivity.

geometry_and_frame: Cartesian x coordinate normal to a slab of thickness L; positive x points from the hot face to the cold face; stationary laboratory frame.
initial_conditions: Not required for the declared steady boundary-value problem; transient approach is excluded.

dependent_variables.name: conductive heat flux
dependent_variables.definition: Energy rate per unit area in the x direction

governing_variables.name: position
governing_variables.sign_convention: 0 at hot face and +x toward cold face

governing_variables.name: thermal conductivity
governing_variables.property_state: constant over the slab state range

conservation_laws: Steady total-energy conservation reduces to d(q_x)/dx=0.
source_and_sink_terms: No volumetric energy generation; energy enters at x=0 and leaves at x=L with equal magnitude.

constitutive_closures.name: Fourier conduction
constitutive_closures.calibration_boundary: k must be measured or independently sourced; it is not fitted to the predicted temperatures

frame_and_invariance: The solid is stationary; translation of the spatial origin leaves the temperature gradient and heat flux unchanged. Relativistic transformations are irrelevant.

ordering_parameters: steady storage/conduction ratio is zero by problem definition
scale_analysis.expected_reduction_error: Zero for the stated mathematical problem; physical error is controlled by violations of one-dimensionality, constant k, perfect boundary temperatures, and zero generation.

baselines: Exact linear temperature solution of the constant-coefficient plane-wall problem
calibration_boundary: No parameter is calibrated to this solution; k, L, T_H, and T_C are independent inputs.
falsification_cases: Measured curvature in T(x) beyond uncertainty
Sensitivity to lateral dimension inconsistent with one-dimensionality
uncertainty_plan: Propagate independent or covariant uncertainty in k, L, T_H, and T_C through q_x=k(T_H-T_C)/L.
benchmark_plan: Substitute the closed form into the ODE and boundary conditions
Compare a numerical discretization against the exact linear profile if code is introduced
provenance: All equations in this package are derived from steady energy conservation and the declared Fourier closure; no experimental validation is claimed.
